merger_description:
Equans Horizon Topco Pty Limited (trading as ‘Equans’) (**Equans ANZ**), proposes to acquire the majority of the issued share capital in Credible Audio Visual Solutions Pty Ltd (**CAVS**) through a share purchase agreement (**the Acquisition**).

In Australia, Equans ANZ is headquartered in Sydney and supplies a broad range of technical services, including electrical (including energy renewable projects and grid connections) and communications installation, facility management services such as the installation and maintenance of heating, ventilation and air conditioning and fire protection products, digital and static signage services and audio-visual (**AV**) integration. Its AV services are provided to government, commercial and industrial customers across Australia. These services are typically delivered as part of larger integrated projects (such as infrastructure upgrades or building services), rather than on a standalone basis.

CAVS is a NSW-based AV design and integration company with one location in Western Sydney. It supplies AV and video conferencing technology services for commercial, government and public sector clients across Australia, primarily in NSW. Its principal activities comprise end-to-end AV services including system design, equipment supply, installation and integration, typically on a standalone basis or as part of technology focused projects.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of AV services to
customers in NSW and Australia is estimated to be low and
the increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
is expected to be small
b. the presence of alternative suppliers in NSW and Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
